Dialogue.Line: These fields... they look like they've been abandoned. What happened here?
We didn't abandon them... not willingly.
Then why are the crops failing?
That's the strange part... they're not. They grow faster than ever.
...That doesn't sound like a problem.
It is when they rot just as fast. Healthy one day, then black and mush the next.
How about the irrigation canals?
Some dried up. Others... carry something foul. We stopped trusting the water.
Has anything like this happened before?
Never. The harvests used to follow the seasons... steady and predictable. Now it's like the land's being forced to grow.
Forced... by what?
They say the Steward's relic keeps the land "blessed."
...but blessings shouldn't feel like this.
...I wonder if we can still earn enough for the next season.
The crops seem to be growing unnaturally. Spots of decay decorate the fields despite their size.
This doesn't seem to be working correctly.
The greenhouse may hold clues about the region's declining harvest. I should search the area for signs of what happened.
The old irrigation system once carried life throughout the region. Restoring its flow may reveal what has been hidden beneath the land.
If the water flows properly again... maybe the truth will surface with it. I need something to clear this.
As water spreads across the farmland, unusual changes begin to appear. Crops wither and the soil darkens.
This isn't what I expected.
The land is trying to tell me something.
They look healthy until you look closer.
Another patch of crops shows the same pattern. Fresh growth covers plants whose roots have already decayed, as if something is forcing them to remain alive.
The roots seem to be dying, but something else keeps the crops standing.
I can probably fix these if I have the right materials...
Requires 3 Lumber Bundles and 3 Stone Piles.
I'm still missing some materials.
The garden requires 3 Lumber Bundles and 3 Stone Piles.
Looks a lot better now.
You've been moving through restricted farmland.
That's not something I overlook lightly.
Then don't overlook this either.
Your land is failing, maybe just not in the way you think.
Our harvests are stable. Our people are fed.
Those are the facts that matter.
But that's only on the surface. The crops seem to grow too fast and then rot.
Well, without intervention, they wouldn't grow at all.
You speak of imbalance. I believe this is all for survival.
But survival built on something unstable won't last long.
Do you know what a failed harvest looks like?
Empty storage. Starving families?
I do, more than anyone else.
And I know what this becomes if it continues.
The Verdant Shard has sustained this region through droughts, blights, and collapse. I will not abandon it based on speculation.
Then let me prove it.
...You're either reckless, or very certain.
If your claims hold any truth... you'll have your proof.
Very well then. Visit our most productive fields.
But if you can't prove it?
You will leave this matter alone.
Visit our most productive fields. Bring me proof, not speculation.
The Steward has granted access to the region's most productive farmland. Although the fields appear healthy, something beneath the surface feels unnatural.
If the truth is here... the land will reveal it.
So this is what was hidden beneath it all.
The harvest was never healthy.
It only looked that way.
I spent years believing the Verdant Shard was protecting this region.
It protected it.
But it wasn't meant to carry the burden alone.
I thought I was preserving our future.
You were trying to.
But forcing the land to keep giving...
only made it weaker.
If this continues...
...there won't be anything left to protect.
No.
No. There won't.
I feared losing our harvest.
But I never realized... we were already losing the land itself.
The Verdant Shard was entrusted to us to preserve balance.
...Not to replace it.
I don't know what tomorrow will bring.
Neither do I.
But if restoring balance gives this land a chance to recover.
Then I will place my trust in you.
Obtained the Verdant Shard.
Unlocked Ability: Spirit Dash.
